facts.fact: Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at Mhow.
He was born into the Mahar community.
He earned a doctorate in economics from Columbia University.
He trained as a barrister at Gray's Inn, London.
He took a D.Sc. from the London School of Economics.
His slogan was 'Educate, Agitate, Organise'.
The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) asserted the right to draw water from a public tank.
The Mahad tank was the Chavdar tank.
The Kalaram Temple Entry Satyagraha (1930) took place at Nashik.
Mooknayak (1920) was his first journal, aided by Shahu of Kolhapur.
He founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924.
Bahishkrit Bharat (1927) was his Marathi fortnightly.
Prabuddha Bharat (1956) was his last journal.
He founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.
He founded the Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942.
He planned the Republican Party of India (launched 1957).
'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) was an undelivered speech for the Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal, Lahore.
He represented the Depressed Classes at the Round Table Conferences.
The Communal Award (1932) gave the Depressed Classes separate electorates.
The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between Gandhi and Ambedkar.
The Poona Pact raised reserved provincial seats from 71 to 148.
M.N. Roy first proposed a Constituent Assembly (1934).
The Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946).
The Assembly was planned with 389 seats.
Ninety-three seats were allotted to the princely states.
After partition its strength fell to 299.
The Assembly was not elected by universal adult franchise.
The Assembly first met on 9 December 1946.
Sachchidananda Sinha was its first (provisional) President.
Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President of the Assembly.
H.C. Mukherjee was Vice-President of the Assembly.
B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor.
Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946.
The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947.
Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947.
Sardar Patel was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee.
The Rules of Procedure Committee was chaired by Rajendra Prasad.
Ambedkar is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
26 January was chosen to honour the 1930 Purna Swaraj pledge.
Framing took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
Durgabai Deshmukh, founder of the Andhra Mahila Sabha, was an Assembly member.
Ambedkar was the first Law Minister of independent India.
He resigned partly over the Hindu Code Bill.
He embraced Buddhism at Nagpur in 1956.
He died on 6 December 1956.
He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.
K.C. Neogy was a member of the Constituent Assembly.
K.C. Neogy chaired the First Finance Commission (1951).
The National Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947.
The National Anthem and National Song were adopted on 24 January 1950.
The State Emblem is the Lion Capital of Sarnath (adopted 26 January 1950).
Framing cost about ₹64 lakh.
Prem Behari Narain Raizada hand-wrote the original Constitution.
Nandalal Bose and his team illustrated the Constitution.
The Assembly served as the provisional Parliament until the first elections.
The Assembly held 11 sessions.
N.G. Ranga was an Andhra member of the Assembly.
Tanguturi Prakasam ('Andhra Kesari') was an Assembly member.
Pattabhi Sitaramayya was an Andhra member of the Assembly.
Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, a Telugu jurist, sat on the Drafting Committee.
Ambedkar called caste a 'division of labourers', not of labour.
The August Offer (1940) conceded the Assembly in principle.
Ambedkar's father Ramji Maloji Sakpal was a subedar in the British Indian Army at the Mhow cantonment.
The family came from Ambadawe village in Ratnagiri district; a teacher changed the surname 'Ambadawekar' to Ambedkar.
A scholarship from Sayajirao Gaekwad III, Maharaja of Baroda, took Ambedkar to Columbia University (1913).
At Columbia he took an MA (1915) and a PhD with the thesis "The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India" (published 1925).
In 1919 Ambedkar testified before the Southborough (Franchise) Committee, demanding separate electorates and reserved seats for the Depressed Classes.
He was nominated to the Bombay Legislative Council in 1926.
In 1928 he gave evidence to the Simon Commission as a member of the Bombay Presidency Committee.
At the Yeola conference (13 October 1935) Ambedkar declared: 'I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu.'
He was the Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council from 1942 to 1946.
Ambedkar entered the Constituent Assembly from Bengal (Jessore–Khulna) with the support of Jogendra Nath Mandal.
After partition took away his Bengal seat, Ambedkar was re-elected from Bombay to the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.
He resigned from the Nehru cabinet in September 1951 over the stalling of the Hindu Code Bill.
In the first general election (1952) he lost the Bombay North seat to N.S. Kajrolkar; he then entered the Rajya Sabha from Bombay.
He founded the People's Education Society (1945), which opened Siddharth College, Bombay (1946) and Milind College, Aurangabad (1950).
On 14 October 1956 at Nagpur the Burmese monk Bhadant U Chandramani administered the Buddhist initiation to Ambedkar, who then gave his followers 22 vows.
Ambedkar died at 26 Alipur Road, Delhi; he was cremated at Chaitya Bhoomi, Dadar (Mumbai), and 6 December is observed as Mahaparinirvan Diwas.
The 'Panchteerth' are Mhow (birth), 10 King Henry's Road London (study), Deekshabhoomi Nagpur, 26 Alipur Road Delhi and Chaitya Bhoomi Mumbai.
'Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development' was a paper Ambedkar read at a Columbia seminar in 1916.
'The Problem of the Rupee' (1923) was his D.Sc. thesis at the London School of Economics.
Ambedkar's evidence on currency fed the Hilton Young Commission (1926), whose report led to the RBI (1935).
'Thoughts on Pakistan' (1940), later 'Pakistan or the Partition of India', analysed the Muslim League's demand.
'Ranade, Gandhi and Jinnah' (1943) was a lecture on Ranade's birth anniversary.
'What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables' (1945) attacked the Congress record on untouchability.
keys: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done

facts.fact: 'Who Were the Shudras?' (1946) traced the origin of the Shudra varna.
'States and Minorities' (1947) was his memorandum to the Constituent Assembly on behalf of the Scheduled Castes Federation.
'The Untouchables: Who Were They and Why They Became Untouchables?' appeared in 1948.
'Thoughts on Linguistic States' (1955) backed linguistic states but warned against very large ones.
'The Buddha and His Dhamma' was published posthumously in 1957.
Mooknayak, Ambedkar's first journal (31 January 1920), means 'Leader of the Voiceless'.
Ambedkar launched the journal Samata in 1928 for the Samaj Samata Sangh.
His journal Janata (1930) was renamed Prabuddha Bharat in 1956.
Vital Vidhvansak (1888), the first Dalit journal, was started by Gopal Baba Walangkar — not by Ambedkar.
Since 2015 (Ambedkar's 125th birth year) 26 November has been observed as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas); it was earlier National Law Day.
The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded in Bombay on 20 July 1924.
The source text dates the 'Depressed Classes Institute' — Ambedkar's Mahar movement body — to 1924.
Ambedkar led the march to the Chavdar tank at Mahad (Kolaba district) on 20 March 1927.
The Manusmriti was burnt at Mahad on 25 December 1927, a day observed as Manusmriti Dahan Din.
The Parvati temple satyagraha at Pune (1929) preceded the Kalaram campaign.
The Kalaram temple satyagraha at Nashik began on 2 March 1930.
At the First Round Table Conference the Depressed Classes were represented by Ambedkar and Rao Bahadur R. Srinivasan.
The Communal Award was announced by British PM Ramsay MacDonald on 16 August 1932.
Gandhi began his fast unto death against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes in Yerawada jail on 20 September 1932.
The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932.
Madan Mohan Malaviya signed the Poona Pact for the caste Hindus, Ambedkar for the Depressed Classes.
The Poona Pact also reserved 18 per cent of the general seats in the central legislature for the Depressed Classes.
After the Pact Gandhi founded the All-India Anti-Untouchability League (1932; later Harijan Sevak Sangh) and the weekly Harijan (1933).
The All-India Scheduled Castes Federation was founded at Nagpur in July 1942.
The Union Powers Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
The Union Constitution Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
The States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with the States) was chaired by Nehru, not Patel.
The Special Committee to Examine the Draft Constitution was chaired by Nehru.
The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Patel.
The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas was chaired by Sardar Patel.
The Steering Committee was chaired by Rajendra Prasad.
The Finance and Staff Committee was chaired by Rajendra Prasad.
The Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag was chaired by Rajendra Prasad.
keys: Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag

facts.fact: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani.
The Minorities Sub-Committee was chaired by H.C. Mukherjee.
The North-East Frontier Tribal Areas and Assam Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas Sub-Committee was chaired by Gopinath Bardoloi.
The Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas (other than Assam) Sub-Committee was chaired by A.V. Thakkar.
The Credentials Committee was chaired by Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar.
The House Committee was chaired by B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
The Committee on Chief Commissioners' Provinces was chaired by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
The Order of Business Committee was chaired by K.M. Munshi.
The Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
The Ad-hoc Committee on the Supreme Court was chaired by S. Varadachari.
The Expert Committee on the Financial Provisions of the Union Constitution was chaired by Nalini Ranjan Ghosh.
The Press Gallery Committee was chaired by Usha Nath Sen.
K.M. Munshi, founder of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1938), was a member of the Drafting Committee.
N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, a former Prime Minister (Dewan) of Jammu and Kashmir, was a member of the Drafting Committee.
Syed Mohammad Saadulla, a former Premier of Assam, was a member of the Drafting Committee.
N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter on the Drafting Committee.
T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (who died in 1948) on the Drafting Committee.
In the July 1946 elections the Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and small groups and independents 15.
The Muslim League boycotted the Assembly, which first met on 9 December 1946 with 211 members.
Members from the provinces were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
The Assembly had two Vice-Presidents: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.
Sachchidananda Sinha presided as the oldest member, following the French practice.
Representatives of six princely States took their seats on 28 April 1947.
B.N. Rau prepared the first draft of the Constitution in October 1947.
The Draft Constitution was published in February 1948.
About 7,635 amendments to the draft were proposed, of which 2,473 were discussed.
Ambedkar introduced the final draft in the Assembly on 4 November 1948 (first reading).
The second (clause-by-clause) reading ran from 15 November 1948 to 17 October 1949.
The third reading began on 14 November 1949; the motion was passed on 26 November 1949.
Over 11 sessions the Assembly sat for 165 days, 114 of them on the Draft.
The original Constitution had a Preamble, 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
Provisions on citizenship, elections, the provisional Parliament and transitional matters came into force on 26 November 1949 itself.
284 members signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950.
On 24 January 1950 the Assembly elected Rajendra Prasad the first President of India.
The Hindi original was calligraphed by Vasant Krishan Vaidya; Beohar Rammanohar Sinha of Nandalal Bose's team decorated the Preamble page.
The elephant was the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly.
The Assembly ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949.
About 15 women sat in the Assembly; Dakshayani Velayudhan was the only Dalit woman and Begum Aizaz Rasul the only Muslim woman.
Hansa Mehta presented the National Flag to the Assembly on behalf of the women of India on 14 August 1947.
Granville Austin called the Constitution 'the cornerstone of a nation' and wrote that 'the Assembly was the Congress and the Congress was India'.
In his speech of 25 November 1949 Ambedkar asked Indians to abandon the 'grammar of anarchy' — civil disobedience and satyagraha — once constitutional methods were open.
His second warning was against hero-worship (bhakti) in politics, 'a sure road to degradation and to eventual dictatorship'.
He warned that on 26 January 1950 India would enter 'a life of contradictions' — equality in politics, inequality in social and economic life.
Ambedkar called Article 32 (constitutional remedies) 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
He described the Directive Principles as a 'novel feature' of the Constitution.
Quoting Grote, Ambedkar said 'constitutional morality' is not natural and has to be cultivated.
Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, the Drafting Committee jurist, was born at Pudur in Nellore district and was Advocate-General of Madras (1929–44).
Durgabai Deshmukh (born Rajahmundry) was the only woman on the Panel of Chairmen of the Constituent Assembly.
Durgabai Deshmukh became the first chairperson of the Central Social Welfare Board (1953).
M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar of Tirupati, an Assembly member, became Speaker of the 2nd Lok Sabha and Governor of Bihar.
Moturi Satyanarayana, an Assembly member from Andhra, was a leader of the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha and active in the official-language debate.
The National Flag adopted on 22 July 1947 was based on the design of Pingali Venkayya of Machilipatnam.
In 'Thoughts on Linguistic States' Ambedkar proposed Hyderabad as India's second capital.
The 125-ft 'Statue of Social Justice' of Ambedkar at Swaraj Maidan, Vijayawada, was unveiled on 19 January 2024.
In 2022 Konaseema district was renamed Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district (HQ Amalapuram).
